Q: Minor Upgrade of Apache Tomcat || from 9.0.56 to 9.0.105 on linux A:

How was Tomcat installed in the first place? If you are using RHEL, perhaps it was installed using the package manager, in which case yum upgrade should probably all you need.

Assuming that you have installed Tomcat yourself, then the instructions on the Apache Tomcat web site regarding upgrading should apply.

I highly recommend reading the section Split Configurations and the linked presentation about why and how to split your deployment to make upgrades (and downgrades) easier.

Q: Simple BERT implementation on R side A:

I implemented the BERT model in R using the R package torch without dependence on Python. The code is available here : https://github.com/ManuHamel/rbert. Here is an example of how the package can be used for classification :

library(torch)
library(rbert)

device <- if (cuda_is_available()) torch_device("cuda") else torch_device("cpu")
obj <- AutoModelForSequenceClassification("bert-base-uncased", num_labels = 2L, device = device)
texts <- c("I love this movie", "This film was terrible", "Excellent acting and great story", "I would not recommend it")
labels <- c(2L, 1L, 1L, 2L)
enc <- bert_batch_encode_plus(obj$tokenizer, texts, max_length = 32L)
ds <- tensor_dataset(
  input_ids = torch_tensor(enc$input_ids, dtype = torch_long()),
  attention_mask = torch_tensor(enc$attention_mask, dtype = torch_long()),
  token_type_ids = torch_tensor(enc$token_type_ids, dtype = torch_long()),
  labels = torch_tensor(labels, dtype = torch_long())
)
dl <- dataloader(ds, batch_size = 2, shuffle = TRUE)
train_sequence_classifier(obj$model, dl, epochs = 3L, lr = 2e-5, device = device)
pred <- predict_sequence_classification(obj, c("I really liked it", "Worst movie ever"), max_length = 32L, device = device)
print(pred$probs)

Q: Sorting sets in an Upset plot A:

keep.order = TRUE preserves the order you pass in sets, but the set size bars (bottom-left) are always plotted based on the order you pas to sets argument.

sets_ordered <- names(sort(colSums(modality_matrix_upset)))

UpSetR::upset(
  modality_matrix_upset,
  nsets = 7,
  sets = sets_ordered,
  order.by = "freq",
  keep.order = TRUE,
  mainbar.y.label = "Number of school",
  sets.x.label = "Number of participant schools"
)
